solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Medieval conjuror converted St Michael

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters of the saint's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sorcerer of the Middle Ages is said to have turned to the saint, or won Michael over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' is the anagram signal, rearranging ST MICHAEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An alchemist of the Middle Ages tried to turn base metals to gold, a figure close to a magician or conjuror.

clue.text: Greek character with company to set up after everything set aside

indicators.note: after places the reversed Greek letter and firm behind the word for everything

parts.note: everything means all

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised, so these letters read bottom to top

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek figure and a firm are to be established once everything else is put to one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to set up' is a down-clue reversal: the Greek letter and the firm read upwards, giving OCATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate is to assign or earmark something for a purpose, which is what setting aside means.

clue.text: Preserve in aspic a nut

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone suggests keeping a nut set in savoury jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the letters inside aspiC A Nut.
explanation.definitionFit: To can food is to preserve it by sealing it in a tin.

clue.text: You round soldiers up as an adversary

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
round means one word surrounds the other

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
soldiers are men in crossword shorthand

explanation.surface: Someone rallies troops against you as if you were the foe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You' is the archaic YE; 'round' then 'up' wraps it round the soldiers and reads the whole upwards, from YMENE.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy is a foe or opponent, a straightforward synonym of adversary.

clue.text: Popular plan, besides, crazy but essential

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: crazy suggests something wild and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A popular scheme is mad but nonetheless vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'besides' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder 'crazy' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indispensable cannot be done without, so it is essential.

clue.text: Label as cold nothing that's hot!

parts.note: a tab is a label or tag
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
O is the shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An exclamation about tagging something as freezing when it is in fact hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a fiery chilli sauce, so it is something spicy hot.

clue.text: Just beat little Philip

definitions.meaning: to beat them narrowly, as in pipped at the post
a pet name for Philip, as for the hero of Great Expectations

explanation.surface: A young Philip only narrowly won.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for narrowly defeating and a familiar short form of a man's name.

clue.text: Plant elm, pine, park oddly in a muddle

indicators.note: in a muddle means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged
oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the word park

explanation.surface: Trees in a park are planted in a chaotic jumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives PR from park; 'in a muddle' rearranges ELM PINE PR.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet pimpernel is a small wild flower, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Plan for bed

definitions.meaning: a small piece of ground for planting, as a vegetable patch

explanation.surface: Someone schemes over where to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a secret scheme and a small patch of garden ground.

clue.text: Oil used by batsmen in Leeds, perhaps?

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
perhaps hints that the city's name may be rearranged

parts.note: batsmen at the crease are said to be in

explanation.surface: A lubricant cricketers at a Yorkshire ground might rub on their bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals rearranging the city to LSEED, and 'in' places the batting side inside. Linseed oil is traditionally rubbed on cricket bats; Leeds hosts Test cricket at Headingley.
explanation.definitionFit: Linseed is pressed for an oil used on wood, including cricket bats.

clue.text: With minimum of brains, I am born with zero as airhead

indicators.note: the minimum of a word here is its first, smallest part, its opening letter

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
O looks like the figure zero

explanation.surface: A self-description by someone born with few brains and no sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A bimbo is slang for an attractive but empty-headed person, the same as an airhead.

clue.text: Wimp is small in outskirts of city

indicators.note: in places these letters within the others
the outskirts of a word are its outer letters

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A weakling is too timid for the city centre and lives on the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Cissy is British slang for a cowardly or effeminate person, a wimp.

clue.text: Plan to have upside-down cakes on a rock!

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside-down means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: tarts are pastries or cakes
a gem is a precious stone, informally a rock

explanation.surface: A recipe for upside-down cake with a rock-hard topping.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning scheme or ruse, so a plan.

clue.text: Remains following the end of brass bands

indicators.note: following places the second piece after the first
the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: ashes are what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A brass band's leftovers are what remains after it stops playing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sashes are long strips of cloth worn round the waist or over the shoulder, a kind of band.

clue.text: Cow cooks in a stew

parts.note: to fry is to cook, so fries means cooks

indicators.note: stew suggests stirring things up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cow fusses over a pot of stew.
explanation.definitionFit: The Friesian is a black and white breed of dairy cattle.

clue.text: Begin to recover, or go round the bend?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for passing the critical point of an illness or crisis
taken literally, to steer round a corner in the road

explanation.surface: Someone either starts getting better or goes mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go round the bend' looks like slang for going crazy, but read literally it is driving round a corner.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for starting to improve and also, literally, steering round a bend.

clue.text: Table way over length, with wood on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside means this word wraps around the others

parts.note: a tree is a source of wood

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A wooden table with a long surface stretched across the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle table is a board laid across supports, so a type of table.

clue.text: Emphasise physical and emotional tension

definitions.meaning: to put weight on a point or syllable
strain on the body or mind

explanation.surface: A note about bodily and mental strain, with a call to underline it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for laying emphasis and a noun for strain on body or mind.

clue.text: Inspiring laughter primarily, bomb as children's author

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so one piece takes the other inside

parts.note: a mine is an explosive device, a bomb

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A writer for the young sets off laughter like a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' means taking in: MINE takes in L.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne wrote the Winnie-the-Pooh books for young readers.

clue.text: Impressionist, figure shrouded by cloak of mist

indicators.note: shrouded by means wrapped inside the other letters
the cloak of a word is its outside letters

parts.note: one is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: An Impressionist painting shows a figure veiled in mist.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was a leading French painter of the Impressionist movement.

clue.text: Military force crazy to depose leader

indicators.note: deposing the leader means removing the word's first letter

parts.note: barmy is British slang for crazy

explanation.surface: An army goes mad and overthrows its commander.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a nation's organised land fighting force.

clue.text: True blues?

definitions.meaning: blue is the colour of Britain's Conservatives, the political party on that wing

explanation.surface: A short question about whether sad songs are genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blues' suggests sadness or music; it is the Conservative party, whose colour is blue.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means correct, and also the conservative wing of politics.

clue.text: Translation of Belgian language

indicators.note: translation changes words into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Belgian text is translated into another tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali is the language of Bangladesh and West Bengal.

clue.text: Turkish general unchanged by uprising?

definitions.note: an Ottoman military commander bore the title ..., a word which reads the same either way

indicators.note: in a down clue, uprising would read the letters upwards, and they stay the same

parts.note: an Ottoman military commander bore the title ..., a word which reads the same either way

explanation.surface: An Ottoman commander keeps his post despite a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' suggests a revolt but here means read upwards; the word reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Aga was an Ottoman title for a military commander or chief officer.

clue.text: Vegetable, one of twelve sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: May is one of the twelve months

explanation.surface: One of a dozen vegetables is returned to the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: The yam is a starchy tuber eaten as a root vegetable.

clue.text: Before tutor, English certainly suffering when reading, perhaps?

indicators.note: before places the following pieces ahead of this one

parts.note: yes means certainly
to train is to tutor or coach

explanation.surface: A student agrees, before a lesson, that study hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is tiredness or ache in the eyes, a common complaint from long reading.
